mainEntity.name: How do I plan a guest apartment suitable for aging parents or multigenerational living?

acceptedAnswer.text: Accommodating multigenerational living requires thoughtful design focused on comfort, privacy, and long-term mobility. Prioritizing universal design elements from the start prevents costly retrofits later. In the bathroom, curbless walk-in showers with slip-resistant tile and reinforced backing for future grab bars are practical upgrades. Doorways and hallways should be planned wide enough to accommodate mobility devices comfortably. Additionally, installing a private exterior entrance alongside an interior connecting door gives aging family members independence while keeping them connected to the main household, and dedicated sound-dampening drywall ensures privacy for all generations.
acceptedAnswer.description: Incorporate universal design features like curbless walk-in showers, wider doors, sound-insulating drywall, and private exterior entryways to balance accessibility with household independence.
